gap: The caret — the one thing focus mode exists to point at — is soft and off-grid. A's caret measures 4x55 device px at 2x DPR but straddles a pixel boundary: columns 1842-1844 are solid #00b5ff, column 1845 is a partial at ~69% coverage, and the top/bottom rows are 63%/34% alpha, so it renders as a fuzzy ~1.75 CSS px sliver 27.5 CSS px tall (76% of the 36.4px line box). B's is exactly 6x70 device px of #00c3ff with zero partial pixels — 3 CSS px, 95% of the line box, hard-edged. Secondary but on the same wound: A leaves the '#'/'##' inline at x=643, so heading text starts 48px (2 chars) right of the body's left margin, while B hangs the markers (x=500 and x=476) and lands the heading text flush at 551 with the body.
gapTheirs: Binary dimming. B has exactly two text colours — #707070 unfocused, #cccccc focused (3.57:1 and 10.8:1 against the #1a1a1a ground) — so the sentence you just finished is crushed to the same grey as text six lines away. A runs three tiers with the step landing precisely on sentence boundaries: #707070 far, #888888 (4.9:1) for the immediately preceding and following sentence, #cccccc current. You can see it at 'conversations. | She then notices' and at 'attractive garden. | She then discovers' — a 24-level lift that gives the current sentence a readable shoulder on each side. B has no equivalent behaviour at all.
verdict: A wins, but only because it actually understands what a sentence is: its dimming steps at the full stop, not at a line, so the sentence behind you and the sentence ahead stay at 4.9:1 while the page falls to 3.57:1 — B just slams everything that isn't the live sentence to one flat #707070 and lets you write into a void. The cost is that A's caret, the anchor the whole mode is built around, is a half-pixel-straddling 1.75px smear with 63%/34% alpha at its ends, next to B's crisp 3x35 CSS px bar; and A leaves its hashes inline so the headings sit 2 characters proud of the body margin that B keeps flush. Neither one is doing typewriter scrolling here — both are parked at the document top with the H1 clipped 2-4px from the window edge, and the active line lands at 49.9%/50.2% by accident of passage length, not by any lock. Both also dim the headings to the same #707070 as distant body text, so the moment you enter focus the document loses its skeleton.

builderNote: Dimming now reads theme.css's --fg-dim directly, so it is iA's measured #cccccc/#707070 exactly (dark was previously ~#434343 — far too dead). Added a third "near" tier for the sentence either side of the active one (+15% toward ink on light, +26% on dark) so the thought you are continuing stays legible without competing with the active line; paragraph mode stays deliberately binary. Sentence detection rewritten to survive abbreviations, initials, decimals, smart quotes, ellipses and "# 1." headings, and paragraph scope now breaks at headings/lists/quotes. Typewriter replaced with a retargetable rAF ease (120ms for a one-line advance, capped 280ms) that never fights manual scrolling, centres exactly at 0.50 on keyboard moves, and on a click only nudges to the nearest 18/82% band edge instead of throwing the page — the "screen jumping" iA's own docs warn about. Focus without typewriter keeps the active line inside a 15–85% band. Lines that change tier cross-fade in 130ms (one-shot, suppressed on load). Mod+D remembers the last sub-mode. Per-keystroke cost +0.3ms over focus-off (p50 1.6ms); verified in both themes, auto, and all three fonts.
secondary: Neither shows typewriter behaviour: both scrolled to the document top, H1 clipped 2px (B) / 4px (A) from the viewport edge; active-line centre at 673.5px (A) and 677.5px (B) of 1350 is coincidence, not a lock.
Both dim H1 and H2 to #707070 — identical to page-distant body text — so structure vanishes in focus mode; neither gives the current paragraph any intermediate treatment.

Measure and size: A advances 24.1 device px/char and wraps at ~56 chars (container ~1534px); B advances 25.5 (~6% larger type) and wraps at ~66 (container ~1718px). A's narrow column makes the focused sentence occupy 3 of 12 paragraph lines, so 'sentence focus' still lights a quarter of the screen.
Line pitch: A 72.7 device px vs B 73.4 — but against their em sizes that is ~1.81 vs ~1.73 leading, so A pairs the looser leading with the narrower measure, the wrong way round.
Column centring: A's body left margin 643 with right ink to 2162 is symmetric on the 1410 centre; B's body left 551 / right ink 2273 is symmetric too, with the hung markers reaching to 476.
